title.narrative: Improved coordination, monitoring and reporting for SIDS

description.narrative: SIDS are a priority group in the 42 C5. Therefore, efforts included in this workplan are dedicated to addressing the vulnerabilities faced by SIDS while adapting them for local and regional contexts. The overall goal is to build resilience using the SIDS Accelerator Programmes as the main mechanism through which actions should be implemented taking into consideration the priorities identified in the UNESCO Operational Strategy for SIDS. Actions will build on the lessons learnt from activities implemented during the COVID19 pandemic, the development of the Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI) and the SAMOA Pathway. They will also be forward looking, taking into consideration the ongoing elaboration of the outcome document for the Fourth International SIDS Conference. All activities will take into consideration Global Priorities Africa and Gender and priority group youth. Coordination, monitoring and reporting The SIDS section will continue to ensure the coordination, monitoring and reporting of SIDS related activities within UNESCO, between UNESCO and the SIDS group through the UNESCO – SIDS Exchange; and the UN system, through the Inter-Agency Consultative Group (IACG) on Small Island Developing States (SIDS). There is a need to enhance collaboration with key UN entities such as UNDESA and UNOHRLLS on issues such as follow up of the Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI) and finalization of the outcome document for the 4th International SIDS Conference as well as the Universities Consortium for SIDS (UCSIS) revitalization.. The SIDS Section will continue working with SIDS programme Sectors focal points for Headquarters and Field Offices and with BSP and CPE to ensure improved visibility, knowledge sharing and resources and partnerships mobilization for the implantation of the Accelerator Programmes (ACEs) . An interactive platform will be developed as a mechanism for sharing proven best practices amongst SIDS for increasing resilience to SIDS. Consequently, at least one project proposal per region will be elaborated in collaboration with relevant Field Offices to mobilize additional funds for the benefit of SIDS in priority areas. UNESCO SIDS Exchange This interaction takes place both with the SIDS Group and since the introduction of the Operational Strategy (in 2023), also with the Group of Friends of SIDS. The first meeting allows SIDS members states with the opportunity to interact directly with the ADGs of the sectors and Directors of relevant UNESCO Field Offices about SIDS activities. Representatives from the group of Friends of SIDS will also be invited to the meeting. The second type of interaction is lead by the ADG Sciences with participation of sectoral Focal Points At least one meeting per constituent will be organized each year. These exchanges will be complemented by regular dialogue with the UNESCO SIDS group on relevant issues. Finalization of the SIDS Resilience Report The SIDS Resilience Report was initiated in 2021 as a recommendation of the review of the UNESCO Plan of Action of the SAMOA Pathway. The report was however not concluded due to several delays. The reports aimed at identifying UNESCO interventions that had led to substantial increase in resilience in the SIDS where they were implemented. SIDS4 and the SIDS Operational Strategy are however great opportunities to disseminate these best practices and as such in 2023 the first phase of the report was initiated to be concluded in the 1st quarter of 2024. A number of case studies will be selected to showcase UNESCO’s contribution in this respect. The report will be printed and shared with all SIDS Member States. SIDS Global High-Level Dialogue The High-level Dialogue Series is a joint UNESCO and SIDS Group initiative aimed at identifying best practices in response to actual challenges faced by SIDS and mobilizing of partnerships and resources to increase resilience of SIDS in UNESCO related domains. At least one UNESCO Dialogue Series webinar will be organized every two years in strategic areas. The third dialogue will be held by November 2025 and will focus on Water Security. Representatives from all SIDS regions will describe challenges and opportunities to finding solutions for improved water governance and management in SIDS, paving the way for follow-up actions at the highest level by UNESCO and its partners, through the active engagement of water experts, policymakers and diplomats. The report of the meeting will be published, followed by concrete interventions for resource mobilization. This activity will be done in collaboration with the relevant Hydrology Division. 4th International SIDS Conference The Fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States will mobilize world leaders in Antigua and Barbuda in 2024, to agree on a new programme of action for the next 10 years aiming at supporting SIDS in attaining the Sustainable Development Goals. UNESCO will participate in the preparatory meetings, the event, and support he organization of the Children and Youth Summit on the margins of the Conference. The activity will encompass (1) support for participation of the Regional Offices of the 3 regions (AIS, Caribbean and Pacific) and HQs; (2) setting up an UNESCO conference stand desk/booth; (3) organizing a number of side events; (4) support the organization of the Children and Youth Forum. Support to Accelarator Programmes 1 and 4 ACE1&4: strengthen climate change education through the IslandWatch programme the IsladWatch is a renewed form of the Sandwatch which build of the challenges and opportunities of this iconic programme. In this context, to enhance citizen science contribution to evidence base monitoring and addressing challenges of the marine and terrestrial environments, contributing to quality data availability and an adaptive ecosystem to respond to perceived trends resilience to climate change. This will include upgrading the approaches to the opportunities offered by online and digital technologies, the expansion of areas and stakeholders engaged in observation, the improved scientific curating and analysis of the data, the improved dialogue between the scientific and policy making communities and the use of the old collected data though AI application . The program is closely linked also with STEM education ACE1: Support universities engagement in climate change and environmental research within the context of the revitalized University Consortium for Small Islands States (UCSIS): UNESCO will continue collaborating with UNDESA, OHRLLS, the University of Delaware and the founding members of the University Consortium of Small Islands (UCSIS) to revitalize the Consortium to enhance the role of higher education in supporting resilience in SIDS. In that regard, UNESCO will support with action-research interventions focusing on regional and intra-regional collaboration for the development of scientific research and training between tertiary institutions in SIDS as a strategy for the revitalization of the UCSIS. Advocacy and participation of SIDS in high level events There are a number of high-level events in which it is important to facilitate the participation of key SIDS leaders as well UNESCO experts from SIDS. These events will facilitate greater advocacy for SIDS in UNESCO’s domains in events such as COP and World Water Forum. Communication and promotional material The SIDS Section will support the elaboration of a Communication and outreach strategy and plan as means to improve the visibility of UNESCO actions and get the buy-in for resources mobilization and positioning of the organization as a UN entity of choice. communication of the important work UNESCO is doing in SIDS. The resources will enable (1) the elaboration a communication and visibility strategy; (2) contribute to the SC online platform (3) showcasing how to develop communication and outreach products. For this purpose a consultancy will be deployed to work in the first place in the support of the SIDS4 UNESCO outreach and in at a later stage to design the Communication Plan and support for training of specialist in the Field Offices in charge of SIDS.
